page: Microsoft Azure E64s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, providing 64 dedicated virtual CPUs across 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory resources total 512.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. Cache structure includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB shared L3 cache. Vector and matrix capabilities are supported via AVX-512 and Intel AMX extensions, including amx_tile and amx_int8 instructions. No local disk storage or physical GPUs are bundled, requiring users to attach Azure remote storage for persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute and high throughput across memory-intensive tasks. In multi-core tests, the instance scored in the top tier for Geekbench multi-core (20,795.0) and top quartile for stress-ng (63,774.19). Potentially uncached 256 MB memory transfers reached 430.32 GB/sec for read and 185.29 GB/sec for write, placing large-block bandwidth in the top ten percent. High transaction capability is reflected in 89.49 million Redis SET operations per second and top-tier PassMark database operations, while CPU-based inference achieved 33.14 tokens per second on a 7B language model.

The absence of integrated local storage creates a clear architectural tradeoff: high persistent storage throughput relies entirely on network-attached Premium Storage capacity. Cost efficiency is determined by high memory density combined with dedicated compute resources, avoiding the expense of dedicated accelerators while providing hardware matrix support for machine learning inference. Workloads aligned with this profile include large in-memory databases, enterprise relational database systems, high-capacity Redis caching layers, and large batch data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E64s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs (32 physical cores) on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, paired with 512.0 GB of RAM. Designed without bundled local storage or GPUs, the instance relies on remote storage and leverages advanced processor extensions such as Intel AMX and AVX-512. Benchmark results highlight top-decile performance in multi-core processing, large-block memory bandwidth exceeding 430 GB/sec, and high-frequency database operations reaching nearly 90 million Redis SET operations per second. The 8.0 GB RAM-per-vCPU density delivers strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy operations, bypassing expensive discrete accelerators while still maintaining robust CPU-based inferencing and high-throughput data tasks. It is technically suited for enterprise in-memory databases, transactional database backends, large caching infrastructures, and data processing engines.
